events.title: Sinhalese Arrival
events.description: Legend says Prince Vijaya from North India and his followers arrived in Sri Lanka, establishing Sinhalese kingdom. Sinhalese became Sri Lanka's main ethnic group.

events.title: Buddhism Introduced
events.description: Mahinda, son of Indian Emperor Ashoka, brought Theravada Buddhism to Sri Lanka. King Devanampiya Tissa converted to Buddhism, making it the state religion. Sri Lanka became a Buddhist holy land.

events.title: Anuradhapura Kingdom
events.description: Anuradhapura became Sri Lanka's capital for 1,400 years. Buddhist culture flourished, constructing magnificent stupas and temples.

events.title: Palm Leaf Manuscript Compilation
events.description: Sri Lankan monks first completely wrote Buddhist scriptures (Tripitaka) on palm leaves, preserving Buddhist texts. Sri Lanka became Theravada Buddhism center.

events.title: Tamil Migration
events.description: Tamils from South India began migrating to northern Sri Lanka, bringing Hinduism and Tamil culture. Tamil-Sinhalese conflict began.

events.title: Sigiriya Rock Palace Built
events.description: King Kashyapa I built Sigiriya Rock Palace, one of world's most spectacular ancient palaces, still an iconic Sri Lankan attraction today.

events.title: Capital Moved to Polonnaruwa
events.description: Due to Tamil invasions, Sinhalese kingdom moved capital from Anuradhapura to Polonnaruwa. Polonnaruwa became new political and cultural center.

events.title: King Parakramabahu the Great
events.description: Parakramabahu I was one of Sri Lanka's greatest kings, unifying whole island, building irrigation projects and Buddhist architecture. Sri Lanka entered golden age.

events.title: Kingdom Fragmentation
events.description: Sri Lanka fragmented into multiple small kingdoms: northern Tamil kingdom (Jaffna) and southern Sinhalese kingdoms. Island fell into division and civil war.

events.title: Portuguese Arrival
events.description: Portuguese explorers arrived in Sri Lanka, attracted by island's cinnamon. Portugal began establishing footholds in coastal areas.

events.title: Portuguese Colonial Rule
events.description: Portugal controlled Sri Lankan coastal areas, monopolizing cinnamon trade, forcibly spreading Catholicism. Many Sinhalese and Tamils forced to convert to Catholicism.

events.title: Kingdom of Kandy Established
events.description: Sinhalese established Kingdom of Kandy in central highlands, becoming last bastion against European colonizers, maintaining independence for nearly 300 years.

events.title: Dutch Conquest of Coastal Areas
events.description: Dutch East India Company defeated Portuguese, occupying Sri Lankan coastal areas. Dutch rule was more systematic than Portuguese, developing cinnamon plantations.

events.title: British Occupation
events.description: During Napoleonic Wars, Britain seized Sri Lanka (then called Ceylon) from Dutch hands.

events.title: Kingdom of Kandy Surrenders
events.description: Britain conquered last independent kingdom Kandy. Entire Sri Lanka became British colony, ending 2,500 years of kingdom history.

events.title: British Colonial Rule
events.description: Britain developed tea, rubber, coconut plantations in Sri Lanka. Imported large numbers of Tamil laborers from South India, intensifying ethnic tensions. Ceylon tea became world famous.

events.title: Tea Plantation Industry Emerges
events.description: Scottish planter James Taylor introduced tea cultivation in Ceylon. Ceylon tea industry rapidly developed, becoming a major global tea exporter.

events.title: Universal Suffrage
events.description: Britain granted Ceylon universal suffrage, first Asian colony to implement universal voting. This laid foundation for post-independence democratic politics.

events.title: Indian Tamil Labor Migration
events.description: Britain imported hundreds of thousands of Tamil laborers from South India to work in tea plantations. These 'Indian Tamils' became a distinct group from local 'Ceylon Tamils'.

events.title: Sri Lankan Independence
events.description: Ceylon gained independence from Britain, becoming a Commonwealth Dominion. Don Stephen Senanayake became first Prime Minister. February 4 became Independence Day.

events.title: Sinhala Only Act
events.description: Bandaranaike government passed act making Sinhala the only official language. Tamil minority strongly opposed, ethnic tensions intensified.

events.title: Indian Tamil Citizenship Issue
events.description: Post-independence government stripped Indian Tamil tea plantation workers of citizenship and voting rights. Hundreds of thousands became stateless.

events.title: Bandaranaike Assassinated
events.description: Prime Minister Solomon Bandaranaike was assassinated by a Buddhist monk. His widow Sirimavo Bandaranaike later became world's first female Prime Minister.

events.title: Rise of Bandaranaike Family
events.description: Solomon Bandaranaike founded Sri Lanka Freedom Party (SLFP). Bandaranaike family began dominating Sri Lankan politics for decades.

events.title: Renamed Sri Lanka
events.description: Country name changed from 'Ceylon' to 'Sri Lanka', severing colonial history symbol. Also became republic, leaving Commonwealth monarchy.

events.title: Black July and Civil War Eruption
events.description: After LTTE attacked government troops, Sinhalese mobs massacred Tamil civilians in Colombo, killing about 3,000. This triggered a 26-year bloody civil war.

events.title: Sri Lankan Civil War
events.description: Government forces and LTTE waged civil war. LTTE sought to establish an independent Tamil state (Tamil Eelam). The civil war killed about 100,000 and displaced hundreds of thousands.

events.title: Indian Peacekeeping Force Intervenes
events.description: India deployed peacekeeping force (IPKF) to Sri Lanka, attempting to mediate conflict. But peacekeeping operation failed, Indian forces instead fought LTTE, withdrawing in 1990.

events.title: Gandhi Assassinated
events.description: LTTE female suicide bomber assassinated former Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in India, retaliating for Indian military intervention. This was one of LTTE's most notorious terrorist acts.

events.title: President Premadasa Assassinated
events.description: President Ranasinghe Premadasa was assassinated by LTTE suicide bomber. This was highest-level assassination in Sri Lankan civil war.

events.title: Airport Attack
events.description: LTTE attacked Colombo International Airport, destroying multiple civilian and military aircraft, causing massive economic losses. This was one of LTTE's boldest attacks.

events.title: Ceasefire Agreement
events.description: Government and LTTE signed ceasefire agreement, Norway mediated. Peace process gave people hope, but ultimately broke down, civil war resumed.

events.title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
events.description: Indonesian earthquake triggered tsunami hitting Sri Lanka, killing about 35,000, leaving 1 million homeless. This was Sri Lanka's worst natural disaster in history.

events.title: Rajapaksa Elected President
events.description: Mahinda Rajapaksa elected president, promising military solution to civil war. He launched all-out offensive to completely eliminate LTTE.

events.title: Civil War Ends
events.description: Government forces launched all-out offensive, annihilating LTTE, killing LTTE leader Prabhakaran. The 26-year civil war ended. However, government forces allegedly committed war crimes in final stages, killing about 40,000 civilians.

events.title: Rajapaksa Authoritarian Rule
events.description: Rajapaksa held long-term power as war hero, family members occupied important positions. Serious corruption, restricted press freedom, opposition and journalists persecuted.

events.title: Regime Change
events.description: Sirisena defeated Rajapaksa, elected president. New government promised democratic reforms and resolution of war crimes issues.

events.title: Easter Terrorist Attacks
events.description: Islamic extremists launched suicide bomb attacks on churches and hotels in Colombo and other cities, killing about 260. This was Sri Lanka's worst terrorist attack since civil war ended.

events.title: Gotabaya Rajapaksa Elected
events.description: Mahinda's brother Gotabaya Rajapaksa (former Defense Minister) elected president. Rajapaksa family regained power.

events.title: Economic Collapse and Popular Uprising
events.description: Sri Lanka fell into severe economic crisis, foreign reserves depleted, unable to pay for imports, fuel, food, medicine shortages. People launched mass protests ('Go Gota' movement), occupying presidential palace.

events.title: COVID-19 and Economic Impact
events.description: Pandemic devastated Sri Lanka's tourism industry (a pillar of economy). Government implemented controversial organic farming policy, banning fertilizer imports, causing agricultural crisis.

events.title: Economic Collapse
events.description: Sri Lanka fell into severe economic crisis: foreign reserves depleted, unable to repay foreign debt, inflation soared, fuel and medicine shortages. Worst economic crisis since independence.

events.title: Mass Protests and Government Collapse
events.description: Hundreds of thousands protested economic crisis and government corruption, occupying presidential and prime ministerial residences. Gotabaya Rajapaksa fled to Singapore and resigned. Rajapaksa family rule ended.

events.title: Wickremesinghe Becomes President
events.description: Ranil Wickremesinghe elected president, inheriting bankrupt nation. Sri Lanka became first Asian country to declare bankruptcy.

events.title: IMF Bailout and Economic Reconstruction
events.description: Sri Lanka received IMF $2.9 billion bailout program. Government implemented austerity measures, economy slowly recovering. But people's lives difficult, high inflation.

events.title: Dissanayake Elected President
events.description: Leftist People's Liberation Front leader Anura Kumara Dissanayake elected president, Sri Lanka's first leftist president, representing people's complete weariness of traditional political families.

events.title: Economic and Political Challenges
events.description: Sri Lanka has population of about 22 million, Buddhist country, main industries tea, tourism, garments. Faces challenges of huge foreign debt, incomplete ethnic reconciliation, war crimes accountability. Economy gradually recovering but political instability continues.
